answer: A proof-of-retrievability protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to store unique heritage datasets, from polar glacier surveys to folios of an Elizabethan sonnet. To authenticate, an agent must decrypt a challenge cipher keyed to random byte offsets in its assigned replica, forcing adversaries to commit scarce non-volatile storage hardware per identity. However, colluding attackers can bypass local storage costs by streaming challenged blocks on demand over high-speed networks.
